constraints_readonly: Changes can only be made in the repo.
constraints_loading: Fetching the rulebook from the service…
constraints_physics_hint: Drives nothing at run time: the kernel computes with constants of its own, checked against this file (src/constraints/physics.json).
constraints_weichen_hint: Form tables of the switches and crossings — maintained in the repo (src/constraints/db-ril-800-0120.json), not fetched from the service: the app draws with them itself.
constraints_weichen_regel_weichen_hint: Ril 800.0120A01 — the forms a design is meant to use. The switch connection reaches here first; within a speed the flatter form comes first, the sharper one is what it falls back to. The symmetrical switch has no through route and is therefore only ever placed by hand.
constraints_weichen_regel_kreuzungen_hin: Ril 800.0120A01. Two straights at the crossing angle; the switch mark can be negative — the two roads stand 2.272 m apart before the body ends.
constraints_weichen_regel_kreuzungsweich: Ril 800.0120A01. Connecting curves between the ends of the crossing roads; the EKW is the DKW with one curve left out. The speed is stated per route: the through road first, then the curves.
constraints_weichen_sonder_weichen_hint: Ril 800.0120A02 — permitted, but not the rule. The switch connection falls back on them when a standard form cannot reach the minimum intermediate straight for the spacing.
constraints_weichen_sonder_kreuzungen_hi: Ril 800.0120A02. Several of them are the crossing two switches of one form make: 1:4.444 = 2 × 1:9, 1:3.683 = 2 × 1:7.5, 1:6.964 = 2 × 1:14.
constraints_weichen_sonder_kreuzungsweic: Ril 800.0120A02 — the curved crossing switches EBKW and DBKW. Their crossing roads curve the same way, their ends lie l_b along those arcs, and their length is 2·l_b. Radius and speed are stated per route: the straight connection, the crossing roads, and in the DBKW the inner curve. The DBKW carries the EBKW's crossing; its own row is not delivered (OP.W.02).
constraints_weichen_symmetrisch: symmetrical — both roads leave the toe on this radius, each through half the angle
constraints_service_down: The optimizer service is not answering — only the bundled rulebooks are listed here.
constraints_querschnitt_hint: Maintained in the repo (src/constraints/db-ril-800-0130.json). The cross section reads its clearance profile from this file.
constraints_querschnitt_strecken_hint: Ril 800.0130, p. 1. The formation width applies to a double-track line without cant: the track spacing plus twice the distance to the formation edge.
constraints_querschnitt_lichtraum_hint: Ril 800.0130A01, p. 2. Dimensions in mm, measured from the track centre and the top of rail (TOR). Dashed: the areas that may be intruded into.
regelwerk_title_db-ril-800-0120: DB Ril 800.0120 | Selection of switches and crossings
regelwerk_title_db-ril-800-0130: DB Ril 800.0130 | Line cross sections on earthworks

table_rules_ok: Every rule that was checked is kept
table_rules_unchecked: Not checked: without a design speed almost every rule is undetermined.
constraints_katalog_hint: Maintained in the repo (src/constraints/), not fetched from the service — and not just to read: these very rules fill the "Rules" column of the element table.

info_description: This tool lets you create track geometry for operational simulations. The data can currently be exported for use in OSRD.
info_layers: Choose the background map that fits as a planning base – for instance OpenStreetMap, aerial imagery or terrain models.
info_places: Plan new, standalone tracks – as a straight line, a curve, or offset in parallel to an existing element or track.
info_connect: Extend existing tracks at their end node with straights or curves, with transition curves and cant where needed.
info_connect_switch: Place plain switches, curved switches, crossings or crossing switches – at the end of an element or inserted into an existing track, across several straights, curves and clothoids if needed. Connect two parallel tracks with a calculated switch connection.
info_splice: Join two straights with an arc, or two arcs with a straight (including clothoids), for a smooth, continuous alignment.
info_edit: Select an element to adjust its length and radius or delete it. For a track you can edit its properties, reverse its direction, open the table editor or delete it.
info_optimize: Raise the achievable speed by improving curve radii within an offset corridor – for a whole track or a single arc, with an optional global optimization (Python).
info_platform: Select a track and two points on it to lay out a platform. Its edges follow the track on the side you choose; you state the height above top of rail.
info_cross_section: Pick an element to see its cross section – the clearance profile the project is designed against, the superstructure of its track, and what cant and curvature do to both.
info_data: Import and export data – as a project file, individual tracks, survey data, CSV, or for OSRD.
info_elevation: Show a track's elevation profile and fill in missing heights automatically from the terrain model.
info_plan: Export a scale plan (1:500/1:1000) as PDF, split across multiple sheets if needed – with title block, scale bar, north arrow and background map.
scurve_no_solution: No solution: the tracks meet at too sharp an angle.
scurve_too_short: Intermediate element shorter than the switch form's minimum.
scurve_too_sharp: Tracks converge too much: the intermediate curve is too sharp for this speed.
scurve_hint_no_bloss: A switch connection cannot lie on a Bloss curve – its pieces are no Bloss curves.
scurve_branch_too_sharp: The turnout bent into the curve gets too sharp for this speed.
scurve_cant_mismatch: The two tracks carry different cant – the middle element would need a ramp.
scurve_cant_over: Cant above 100 mm: no turnout may be laid there.

cross_section_sleeper_default: Default: sleeper over the whole track
cross_section_use_switch_zone: 15 m before and after a switch
cross_section_reach_hint: How far either side of the track other tracks are drawn
cross_section_terrain_no_height: Terrain cannot be placed: no track in the section has a height

elevation_hint: Click a track on the map, or pick one from the list, to see its profile. The gradient is not determined automatically: a track without one can have it computed from the height data in the profile (the Länder's DGM1, DGM5 of the BKG, MapTiler Terrain outside Germany). Heights edited by hand stay until the track is reloaded.

elevation_compute_missing: There is no height data along this track.
elevation_compute: Compute the gradient from the height data
terrain_source_hint: Where the terrain is read from — for the cross section and for the gradient

elevation_delete_hint: The first and the last point stay — that is where the height meets the joined tracks.
elevation_vcurve_hint: Radius of the vertical curve at the gradient change in m; 0 removes it.

plan_logo_failed: The logo could not be read.
plan_schematic_legend: Schematic overview – only lengths along the line are to scale, track spacing is not
plan_schematic_crowded: Too many tracks side by side – narrow the corridor or choose another reference track.
plan_schematic_km_missing: No kilometrage line in the project – the ruler then shows the chainage along the reference track.
plan_range_hint: empty: kilometrage of the sheet, where known
plan_sketch_auto: Without an image the sketch shows the track network with the sheet outlined in red.
switch_status_hint: Click a switch on the map.
plan_party_signs: Line for place, date and signature
buffer_stop_none: The project has no free track end.
buffer_stop_none_existing: The project has no buffer stop.
buffer_stop_brake: Braking distance behind the buffer stop (m)
buffer_stop_hint: The buffer stop is 2.20 m long and stands on the track; behind it the braking distance runs to the track end. The track itself does not change.
buffer_stop_brake_invalid: The braking distance must be a number of 0 or more.
buffer_stop_too_short: The track is too short: buffer stop and braking distance need {need} m, the track has {have} m.
data_exchange_mdb_buffer_stops: Buffer stops: {{n}} placed on free track ends, {{missed}} without a free track end nearby. The database states neither type nor braking distance – they stand at the track end with no braking distance until set under Edit → Edit buffer stop.
topology_mark_boundary_hint: Mark as the boundary of the planning area: the line runs on here but is not drawn. The end then no longer counts as open.
topology_hint: Click a switch: the tracks connected to it are highlighted. Click a track: the switches it runs into.
info_topology: Shows the track network as a topology: tracks as lines, switches as circles, open track ends in red, over a pale map. A track end is connected or free. Clicking a switch highlights its tracks in colour, clicking a track its switches. The topological connections can be shown as an evenly spaced diagram, one per connected network; a click in it zooms the map to the tracks. Open ends can be marked as the boundary of the planning area.

topology_delete_loose_confirm: Delete all {n} tracks without connection? Ctrl+Z undoes it.

compare_zoom_hint: Click an entry to zoom to it on the map.
